```markdown
## Design Decision
### Decision 1: refresh the ARIA state when the dropdown module hides
**Decision:** In `delegateDropdownModule` in `dropdown.ts`, wrap the Fomantic dropdown module's own `hide` method. The wrapper calls the original `hide` with the same arguments, then calls `deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem(100)`. The 100 ms delay matches the `blur` listener, which waits for the hide animation. Confirmed by the implementer, @Jack-Donohue.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Wrap Fomantic's `onHide` setting, the way the function wraps `onLabelCreate`. This was the first proposal. A later `dropdown('setting', {onHide})` call replaces the wrapper, because Fomantic merges new settings over old ones (`dropdown.js:3732-3736`). The label picker makes that call (`repo-issue-sidebar-combolist.ts:231-236`), and so do the `.jump` dropdowns (`common-page.ts:73-81`). The fix would miss the exact picker this issue is about.
- (b) Add Escape to the `keyup` listener that refreshes the state on arrow keys.
- (c) Watch the menu's `class` attribute with a `MutationObserver`, and refresh the state on every change.

**Rationale:** Escape and every other internal close call `module.hide()` (`dropdown.js:1649-1651`). Calls such as `$dropdown.dropdown('hide')` also go through the same module object, so one wrapper catches every hide. It isn't a setting, so later `setting` calls can't replace it, and `dropdown.ts:133-147` already patches the module the same way for `set.direction`. Option (b) is smaller but fixes only Escape. Option (c) catches every hide, but it runs on every animation class change and adds an observer to every dropdown on the page.

**Consequences:** `module.hide()` still calls `settings.onHide` itself, so the label picker's save (`repo-issue-sidebar-combolist.ts:209-211`) runs unchanged. The existing e2e test `issue labels can be selected and deselected by keyboard` checks this, since it presses Escape and checks the saved list. The patch depends on a Fomantic internal method name, the same risk the `set.direction` patch already carries. A Fomantic upgrade must recheck both. The fix PR adds a Vitest case in `dropdown.test.ts` and removes the `test.fail()` line from `tests/e2e/multiselect-aria.test.ts`.

```

```markdown
fix(dropdown): report the label picker collapsed after Escape (#104)

Closes #104

## What changed
The Fomantic ARIA patch in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts` now wraps each dropdown module's own `hide` method. After the original `hide` runs, the wrapper schedules the existing `refreshAriaActiveItem` 100 ms later. That is the same delay the `blur` listener uses for the hide animation. The e2e test that recorded the bug no longer carries `test.fail()`.

## Why
The label picker in the issue sidebar kept `aria-expanded="true"` after Escape closed its list, so a screen reader announced it as expanded. Only the `focus`, `blur`, `mouseup` and arrow-key `keyup` listeners refreshed the attribute. When Escape closes the list, focus stays on the picker, so none of them run.

The issue first proposed wrapping the `onHide` setting. The sidebar pickers set their own `onHide` after the patch runs (`repo-issue-sidebar-combolist.ts:231-236`), and Fomantic merges new settings over old ones, so that wrapper would have been replaced. Wrapping the module method avoids that, because Escape (`dropdown.js:1649-1651`) and `dropdown('hide')` both go through it. The picker's own `onHide`, which saves the labels, still runs inside the original `hide`.

This fixes the Expected Behavior in #104: `aria-expanded` becomes `false` when Escape closes the list.

## How it was tested / Test strategy
- **Unit (Vitest), new:** two tests in `dropdown.test.ts`, under "expanded state on hide". They build a combobox dropdown that sets its own `onHide` after init, as the label picker does. One closes it with Escape and the other with `dropdown('hide')`. Each checks that `aria-expanded` is `"false"` 100 ms later, and the Escape test checks that the picker's `onHide` ran exactly once. Both failed before the fix (`expected 'true' to be 'false'`) and pass after it.
  - The test dropdown has a hidden input in place of the picker's search box. happy-dom moves focus into a search box when the list opens, and blurring that box on hide would trigger the old `blur` refresh and hide the bug. In the browser, focus stays on the picker, which the e2e test checks.
- **E2E (Playwright), changed:** removed `test.fail()` from `issue label picker reports collapsed after Escape` in `tests/e2e/multiselect-aria.test.ts`. It now passes in a real browser on the real issue page. The existing `issue labels can be selected and deselected by keyboard` test presses Escape and checks the label is saved, so it covers the risk named in the issue's Consequences.

Unit tests come first because the cause sits in one module that can be tested without a server. The e2e test confirms the real picker, whose focus behaviour happy-dom doesn't reproduce.

## CI / manual verification

## Design
Follows the revised Decision 1 in #104 (wrap the module's `hide`, not the `onHide` setting), confirmed after the spec review.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** The fix replaces a Fomantic internal method (`module.hide`) rather than using a public callback. A Fomantic upgrade that renames or restructures `hide` would silently undo it. The unit tests would catch that. The existing `set.direction` patch in the same function carries the same risk.

**Encountered:** `dropdown.ts` keeps `aria-expanded` up to date by re-reading the menu's classes from timers scheduled by several DOM listeners, rather than from Fomantic's show/hide lifecycle. That is why this hide path was missed. I added the missing path and didn't restructure the rest, since #25 plans to move the label picker off Fomantic. The file's own TODO, that multiple selection is only partly supported, still stands.
```
